claims.text: The sharp, hysteretic magnetocaloric response in as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys is governed by localized lattice strain and compositional disorder that pin the magnetostructural transformation.
Mild post-deposition annealing can reduce strain heterogeneities and relieve local stresses without forming secondary phases.
Relieving local stresses lowers the energy barriers for the magnetostructural phase change.
Strain-relieving annealing will reduce hysteresis and broaden the entropy-change response over a wider temperature window.
The as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloy is in a single-phase ordered hexagonal state.
The as-deposited alloy contains intrinsic lattice strain and compositional disorder.
A controlled low-temperature annealing treatment should be applied while preserving the overall phase and microstructural features.
Annealing should be conducted under an inert atmosphere below the onset temperature for secondary-phase precipitation.
Local elastic strains and defect pinning sites influence nucleation and propagation of the magnetostructural transformation.
Annealing reduces pinning of domain walls or magnetostructural transformation fronts.
Reduced pinning facilitates a more homogeneous and gradual phase transformation.
A more homogeneous and gradual transformation smooths the magnetocaloric transition and minimizes hysteretic losses.
Annealed specimens will have a broader magnetocaloric transition and lower hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing may moderately reduce the peak magnitude of the magnetocaloric effect because of a trade-off between an abrupt transformation and smoother cycling.
Annealing will improve dynamic cycling performance.
The baseline ingots and microribbons exhibit a sharp, hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition.
The baseline ingots and microribbons have limited heat-exchange rates.
The predicted behavior is limited to annealing conditions that avoid secondary-phase formation and preserve mechanical stability.
The predicted behavior is limited to low-applied-field cycles near the intrinsic magnetostructural transition temperature.
Failure to obtain both a statistically significant hysteresis reduction and observable broadening or smoothing relative to an untreated same-batch control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described generically as an as-deposited alloy, whereas the baseline is described as 'as-deposited ingots and microribbons.' Ingots are ordinarily produced by melting rather than deposition, and this wording conflates the proposed deposited material with earlier bulk or melt-spun forms.
